newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble stable leashed by central bank rates.
newsitem.headline: Rouble stable leashed by central bank rates.

text.p: The rouble was little changed after the central bank further narrowed the spread on its bid/offer rates but dealers said rouble demand was higher ahead of Wednesday's Treasury bill auction.

The central bank said it had set 5,416/5,426 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Monday. Over the last two weeks the central bank has narrowed the spread from the previous 40 points, bringing the rate at which it is willing to buy dollars closer to the rate at which it buys roubles.

"(Given the closer bid/offer rates) banks prefer to close their positions as soon as possible fearing they will not be able to do so if the trend changes," Moscow Business World Bank dealer Nikolay Zolotaryov said.
"But it is a psychological influence rather than something else," he added.
The central bank sets daily bid and offer rates for its operations with major commercial banks, within a broader pre-announced 600-point daily corridor.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,417-20 per dollar compared with an early 5,419-22 and 5,420-23 late on Friday. Tomorrow roubles were stable at 5,421-23 per dollar compared with Friday's late level.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 30-40 percent compared with 10-15 percent late on Friday.
Dealers said the higher overnight rates could be due to speculative bidding and Wednesday's T-bill auction.
"It looks like a speculative trend and rates could fall back tonight," one dealer said.
But Zolotaryov said some commercial banks were building up funds for the T-bill auction which made today and tomorrow rates edge up.
On Wednesday, October 9, the central bank is auctioning 10 trillion roubles of six-month bills.
